newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Seven Network says committed to MGM.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Seven Network says committed to MGM.

text.p: Australian television broadcaster Seven Network Ltd said on Wednesday it remained committed to its investment in the Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer (MGM) studios, rejecting recent media speculation that it was unhappy with its holding.
"A business plan for the future development of Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer has been implemented," Seven said.
"MGM is performing according to this business plan, and contrary to reports in Daily Variety and The Sydney Morning Herald, Seven is happy with its investment in the company."
Seven managing director Gary Rice said MGM formed a core element in a strategy to further strengthen and develop Seven.
"The suggestion that Seven is contemplating selling its investment in the studio is incorrect," he said in a statement.

"We are pleased with the progress of our investment. The past two months has seen MGM - under its new ownership - put in place the plans for its future development in film and television production," Rice said.

Seven chairman Kerry Stokes said Seven's involvement in the acquisition of MGM was a tangible indication of the company's pursuit of business strategies which involved the development Of significant partnerships to secure a major presence in the production and distribution of entertainment software.

"MGM forms a major part of a long-term strategy to allow Seven to further develop presence in the growing international communications industry - from the platform of programme supply," Stokes said in the same statement.
"Seven's investment in MGM followed extensive consideration of the future benefits of the company's involvement in a major Hollywood studio," he said.
"Our position is clear - we are not selling MGM, we are happy with our investment and the studio is performing according to its business plan," Stokes said.
Stokes said production had started on the next James Bond movie, Bond 18, and a production schedule encompassing 12 movies for release over the coming 12 months was well advanced.
This production slate of 12 theatrical motion pictures was foreshadowed at the time of Seven's investment in MGM, he said.

The studio's roster of movie releases in 1996 and development costs for many future projects formed part of the assets of MGM when the company was acquired by Seven in partnership with Kirk Kerkorian's Tracinda Corp, he said.

"Contrary to the report in Daily Variety and The Sydney Morning Herald, neither Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer nor the joint venture investment partners in the studio are seeking further production funding," Stokes said.
The current business plan - agreed to by Seven and Tracinda Corp - provides sufficient funding to support the current business plan for MGM, he said.

Stokes said that in television, the company had two new series in production - Fame LA and Stargate. Both programmes have received significant commitments in major markets and will complement the studio's current schedule of programmes including
The Outer Limits and Poltergeist - The Legacy.
"The company is also negotiating a number of programming agreements with major broadcast and subscription television networks in Europe, North America and Asia," Stokes said.
"The rapidly increasing number of viewing options - particularly Europe and the United States - is placing demand on programming fox those channels," Stokes said.

"As a result, there has been a rapid increase in the prices paid for programming - in particular, movies. Seven's investment in MGM will allow the company to participate in this continuing growth," he said.
Seven invested US$250 million in the deal to take over MGM and Tracinda $600 million.
